verdict: Home Depot's sales fell 3.8% to $38.2B — mostly because last year's quarter had an extra week worth about $2.5B — while comparable sales rose 0.4% and profit came in at $2.6B.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: -3.8% YoY — against a 14-week quarter last year

segments.name: Net sales
segments.note: Everything sold through 2,359 Home Depot stores and its website, plus over 1,250 SRS locations — the professional-supply business Home Depot has been buying to win more contractor spending. This quarter had 13 weeks; the same quarter last year had 14.

flow.costPlain: What Home Depot paid suppliers for the merchandise it sold, plus the cost of getting it into stores.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Store payroll, rent, advertising and running the head office.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of stores, warehouses and equipment over their useful lives.

otherDetail: Interest and other, net was a $551M cost: $594M of interest expense on Home Depot's debt, partly offset by $43M of interest and other income.
follow100Note: Two-thirds of every $100 goes straight back out as the cost of the merchandise itself — retail keeps a much thinner slice than software does. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Underlying demand held steady
takeaways.text: Comparable sales rose 0.4% (0.3% in the U.S.). Management said demand was relatively stable through the year once storms are accounted for, despite consumer uncertainty and pressure in housing.

takeaways.title: The extra week explains the decline
takeaways.text: Sales fell 3.8% and EPS fell to $2.58 from $3.02 — but last year's quarter ran 14 weeks, and that extra week added about $2.5B of sales and roughly $0.30 of EPS. On a like-for-like basis the quarter was close to flat.

takeaways.title: Guidance: a modest 2026
takeaways.text: For fiscal 2026 Home Depot guided to total sales growth of about 2.5% to 4.5%, comparable sales flat to +2%, and diluted EPS roughly flat to +4% — and raised the quarterly dividend 1.3% to $2.33.

oneTimers: The comparison is distorted by the calendar: fiscal 2024's fourth quarter had 14 weeks versus 13 this year. The extra week added approximately $2.5B of sales and about $0.30 of diluted EPS to last year's quarter.
